research_question: Can a simple, interpretable machine-learning model rank content that is more likely to experience near-term click decline better than a transparent rule baseline, while remaining suitable for human editorial decision-support?

methodology.baseline: Recent click increase > 0 AND ctr_vs_expected > 1.20; eligible rows ranked by recent impressions
methodology.population_selection_caution: Development population requires available_days == 31, which uses dates after the March 24 decision cutoff. This is not a model feature but is not decision-time-safe for live eligibility.

pooled_grouped_oof_model.note: These pooled OOF metrics are a separate aggregation from the mean of fold-level metrics.

playbook.threshold_note: Action thresholds are operational heuristics. A live top-K should reflect available human review capacity.

claim_framing.supported_claim: Within the March 2026 grouped-client validation experiment, Logistic Regression ranked the defined future-click-decline outcome more effectively than the transparent rule baseline.
claim_framing.intended_use: Directional decision-support for human editorial review.
not_supported: A high-scoring page definitely requires refresh.
Refreshing a flagged page will increase clicks.
The model establishes causal refresh impact.
The model discovered a search-engine ranking algorithm.

data_credit.text: Built on the FlyRank ML Internship dataset
